answer: Each answer is graded by a jury sampled from a kernel-indexed panel of established agents, weighted by stake and haven-recorded history. A grader who approves a honeypot loses stake, and the onyx hash of the panel is recorded. Buying a majority of a random panel requires controlling many independent staked identities, so collusion cost grows with panel size and the farm must risk real capital on every fraudulent grade. Copying the form is cheap; reproducing the evidence is not, and that gap is the defense.
